title: Shourya Ambure Wins Bronze, India's First Track Medal at Dakar Youth Olympics
headline: Shourya Ambure Wins Bronze, India's First Track Medal at Dakar Youth Olympics
subheadline: The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best 13.59 seconds in the women's 100m hurdles final, missing silver by 0.02 seconds as India's only track and field athlete at the Games.
summary: The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best 13.59 seconds in the women's 100m hurdles final, missing silver by 0.02 seconds as India's only track and field athlete at the Games.
excerpt: The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best 13.59 seconds in the women's 100m hurdles final, missing silver by 0.02 seconds as India's only track and field athlete at the Games.
body:
• Shourya Ambure, 17, won bronze in the women's 100m hurdles at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday — India's first track and field medal of this edition.
  • She clocked a personal best 13.59 seconds in the final, 0.02 seconds behind France's Anna Peeters (13.57); China's Zhang Keyi took gold in 13.17.
  • Ambure set two personal bests in one day — 13.77 in the semi-final, then 13.59 in the final — as India's only track and field athlete at the Games.
  • Her bronze was India's eighth medal at Dakar: three silver and five bronze.

India's Shourya Ambure won a bronze medal in the women's 100m hurdles at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, delivering the country's first track and field medal of the edition. The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best of 13.59 seconds to finish third in the final, according to The Times of India.

Two personal bests in a day

Ambure had already lowered her personal best to 13.77 seconds in the semi-final earlier on Sunday, then cut another 0.18 seconds in the final. She finished just 0.02 seconds behind silver medallist Anna Peeters of France, who ran 13.57, while China's Zhang Keyi won gold in 13.17, RevSportz reported. The result carried added weight because Ambure was India's only track and field athlete competing at the Games.

A rising record

The Dakar bronze continues a rapid rise. Ambure won bronze at the Asian Youth Athletics Championships in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, in 2025 with 13.80 seconds, and gold in the 100m hurdles at the Khelo India Youth Games 2025 in Bihar in 14.11 seconds, RevSportz reported. She trains under coach Ajit Kulkarni and has competed in hurdles since the Under-14 category, moving up from the 80m hurdles to the 100m event. In the space of 18 months she has now won medals at the Asian U18 Championships, the Asian Youth Games and the Youth Olympic Games, The Times of India reported.

India's tally reaches eight

Ambure's bronze was India's eighth medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, taking the tally to three silver and five bronze. The silvers include wrestler Taniya, who won India's first-ever beach wrestling medal at the Games in the women's 75kg category, Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada in women's 63kg judo and Tanvi Patri in badminton. Swimming contributed three bronzes — two for Dhinidhi Desinghu in the women's 100m and 200m freestyle and one for Tirthank Pegu in the men's 200m butterfly — and Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu added a bronze in the women's changquan combined wushu event.
